# Memory Grain (memorygrain.org) - Open Memory Specification
# Full content index for AI language models and crawlers
# Version 1.5 - August 2026
# License: CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain Dedication)

================================================================================
## OVERVIEW
================================================================================

The Memory Grain (.mg) format is an open binary standard for atomic, immutable
knowledge units produced and consumed by autonomous systems. It is to agent
memory what .git objects are to version control.

Design goals:
- Content-addressed (SHA-256 hash IS the unique ID  -  no server needed)
- Immutable (any modification produces a new address)
- Portable (self-describing binary; reads anywhere, no external schema)
- Compliance-ready (GDPR crypto-erasure, HIPAA PHI routing, CCPA disclosure)
- Scale-independent (512-byte IoT grain to 1MB server grain; same format)

Primary use cases:
- AI agents: durable memory across restarts, context window overflow
- Autonomous vehicles: lidar observation recording, incident reconstruction
- Robotics: cross-fleet knowledge sharing, OTA continuity
- IoT sensors: deterministic binary at 10Hz, hardware SHA-256
- Healthcare AI: HIPAA PHI routing without payload deserialization
- Enterprise: SOX-compliant tamper-evident audit trail

================================================================================
## BINARY FORMAT SPECIFICATION (v1.5)
================================================================================

### Fixed 9-Byte Header

Every .mg blob begins with this 9-byte fixed header:

  Byte 0: Version       -  0x01 (the only valid value; any other byte -> ERR_VERSION)
  Byte 1: Flags         -  bitmask (see below)
  Byte 2: Type          -  0x01=Fact, 0x02=Event, 0x03=State,
                         0x04=Workflow, 0x05=Tool, 0x06=Observation,
                         0x07=Goal, 0x08=Reasoning, 0x09=Consensus, 0x0A=Consent,
                         0x0B=Skill, 0x0C=Recommendation
                         0x0D-0xEF: reserved; 0xF0-0xFF: domain profile types
  Bytes 3-4: NS Hash    -  first two bytes of SHA-256(namespace string, UTF-8), uint16 big-endian
  Bytes 5-8: Created    -  uint32 big-endian epoch seconds (range: 1970-2106)
                         COARSE routing hint only; authoritative timestamp in payload (timestamp_ms)

### Flags Byte (Byte 1) Bit Layout

  Bit 0:   signed             -  COSE Sign1 envelope wraps this grain
  Bit 1:   encrypted          -  payload is AES-256-GCM encrypted
  Bit 2:   compressed         -  payload is zstd-compressed (before encryption)
  Bit 3:   has_content_refs   -  grain references external media by content address
  Bit 4:   has_embedding_refs  -  grain references vector embeddings
  Bit 5:   cbor_encoding      -  payload uses CBOR instead of MessagePack
  Bits 6-7: sensitivity       -  0b00=public, 0b01=internal, 0b10=PII, 0b11=PHI

### Sensitivity Routing (bits 6-7)

  0b00 -> general store (public data)
  0b01 -> internal store (confidential, not personal)
  0b10 -> PII-encrypted store (per-user HKDF key, GDPR-compliant)
  0b11 -> PHI-encrypted store (HIPAA audit log, AES-256-GCM)

Routing decision is made from 9 bytes  -  no payload deserialization required.

### Payload (Bytes 8+)

Default: MessagePack (canonical, sorted keys, NFC strings, null-omission).
Optional: CBOR (set bit 5 of flags byte).

Minimum valid blob: 10 bytes (9-byte header + 0x80 empty MessagePack map).
Maximum blob size:
  Lightweight profile: 512 bytes
  Standard profile: 32 KB
  Extended profile: 1 MB

### Content Address

  content_address = lowercase_hex(SHA-256(blob_bytes))

The content address is the identity of the grain. Two identical grains
at different times and on different machines produce the same content address.
A one-bit change anywhere in the blob produces a completely different address.

### Immutability Boundary (v1.2)

A grain has two distinct layers with different mutability guarantees:

  Blob (immutable): 9-byte fixed header + MessagePack/CBOR payload
     -  Covered by content address and COSE signature
     -  Never modified after write

  Index (mutable): Status and access-tracking fields managed by the store
     -  NOT covered by content address or COSE signature
     -  Updated by store on reads or lifecycle events

Index-layer fields: superseded_by, system_valid_to, verification_status,
                    rec_status, access_count, last_accessed_at

Writers MUST NOT embed index-layer fields in the blob payload.
Stores MUST NOT recompute content addresses when index-layer fields change.

================================================================================
## TWELVE GRAIN TYPES (OMS v1.5)
================================================================================

Type byte values are stable across versions. v1.4 renamed two types WITHOUT
changing their bytes, so every existing content address remains valid:

  "belief" -> "fact" (0x01)
  "action" -> "tool" (0x05)

Legacy "belief"/"action" type strings are NOT accepted. Writers MUST emit v1.5
canonical names. (The v1.0 names fact/episode/checkpoint/tool_call were renamed
in v1.2 to belief/event/state/action; v1.4 restored "fact" and settled on "tool".)

### 0x01  -  Fact
A (subject, relation, object) semantic triple with confidence and source.
The canonical unit of declarative knowledge.

Required fields:
  type: "fact"
  subject: string
  relation: string
  object: string | map
  confidence: float 0.0-1.0
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Optional: namespace, user_id, source_type, provenance, structural_tags,
  author_did, temporal_type, valid_from, valid_to, epistemic_status,
  verification_status, processing_basis, identity_state, embedding_text

Example:
  { "type": "fact", "subject": "agent-001", "relation": "knows",
    "object": "route:depot-to-dock-7", "confidence": 0.97,
    "namespace": "navigation", "created_at": 1739980800000 }

### 0x02  -  Event
Raw, timestamped record of something that happened  -  a message, interaction,
utterance, or behavioral occurrence.

Required fields:
  type: "event"
  content: string (raw text; MAY be omitted if subject/relation/object describe the event)
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Optional: role ("user"|"assistant"|"system"|"tool"), content_blocks (array),
  model_id, stop_reason, token_usage, parent_message_id (content address of
  preceding message for threading), consolidated, run_id, session_id,
  all common fields

Example:
  { "type": "event", "role": "assistant",
    "content": "Emergency braking at Hwy 101 MP-42  -  pedestrian detected.",
    "created_at": 1740000023000, "namespace": "driving:safety" }

### 0x03  -  State
Agent state snapshot  -  the portable save point at a moment in time.

Required fields:
  type: "state"
  context: map (agent state snapshot)
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Optional: plan (array[string]), history (array[map]), all common fields

Example:
  { "type": "state", "context": { "case": "claim-7291", "step": 4 },
    "created_at": 1740020000000 }

### 0x04  -  Workflow
Directed graph of procedural steps  -  plans, pipelines, and multi-path processes.
Redesigned in v1.4: the flat `steps` array was replaced by a graph model.

Required fields:
  type: "workflow"
  nodes: array[string] (non-empty; unique IDs that double as human-readable labels)
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Optional:
  trigger: string  -  condition that activates this workflow
  edges: array[map]  -  { src, dst, cond?, max_cycles? }
  bindings: map[node_id -> Tool definition grain hash]
  retries: map[node_id -> max repeat count on failure]
  all common fields

Structural semantics are INFERRED from topology, never declared:
  - multiple outgoing unconditional edges  -> parallel fan-out (fork)
  - node targeted by multiple edges        -> AND-join (all predecessors complete)
  - multiple outgoing conditional edges    -> decision point
  - no outgoing edges                      -> terminal node
  - entry point                            -> first element of `nodes`
  - back-edges allowed only when bounded by max_cycles or retries

Node-to-Tool resolution is three-tier: Bound (node ID in `bindings`  -  fetch the
Tool definition grain by hash), Named (a Tool definition grain with a matching
tool_name), Abstract (node label is a human-readable instruction for the executor).

Executing a node writes a Tool grain related by mg:step_action:<node_id> to the
Workflow hash, so execution records never modify the immutable plan.

Example (fork/join with a bounded retry):
  { "type": "workflow", "trigger": "release requested",
    "nodes": ["build", "unit_test", "lint", "stage_deploy"],
    "edges": [ {"src": "build", "dst": "unit_test"},
               {"src": "build", "dst": "lint"},
               {"src": "unit_test", "dst": "stage_deploy"},
               {"src": "lint", "dst": "stage_deploy"} ],
    "bindings": { "stage_deploy": "sha256:def333..." },
    "retries": { "stage_deploy": 3 },
    "created_at": 1740016400000 }

### 0x05  -  Tool
A record of a tool invocation, code execution, or computer-use action.
Uses tool_phase discriminator: "definition" | "call" | "result" | absent=complete.

Required fields:
  type: "tool"
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)
  (phase-dependent required fields; see §27.1)

Key fields:
  input    (NOT arguments/args  -  removed in v1.2)
  content  (NOT result/res      -  removed in v1.2)
  is_error (NOT success/ok      -  removed in v1.2; inverted polarity)

Other fields: tool_phase, tool_call_id, call_batch_id, tool_type, tool_version,
  execution_mode ("function_call"|"code_exec"|"computer_use"),
  code, stdout, stderr, exit_code, interpreter_id, error_type,
  input_schema, strict,
  output_schema (JSON Schema draft-07 describing the return value; v1.3)

Example:
  { "type": "tool", "tool_name": "portfolio.rebalance",
    "input": { "account": "401k-primary", "target_bonds": 0.4 },
    "content": { "status": "executed", "trades": 3 },
    "is_error": false, "duration_ms": 847, "created_at": 1740012800000 }

### 0x06  -  Observation
Raw sensory or cognitive input  -  what an observer perceived at a moment in time.
Epistemological note: "I perceived X" (Observation) vs "X is true" (Fact).
Also the carrier for Recommendation lifecycle audit grains (§8.12.1), where
observer_type is "human" or one of "rec:agent" / "rec:policy" / "rec:system".

Required fields:
  type: "observation"
  observer_id: string (unique identifier of observing entity)
  observer_type: string (registered type from §24)
  subject: string (entity being observed)
  object: any (observation reading)

Optional: confidence, namespace, observation_mode, observation_scope,
  observer_model, observer_did, epistemic_status, all common fields

Example (physical):
  { "type": "observation", "observer_id": "lidar-front-01",
    "observer_type": "lidar", "subject": "vehicle-003",
    "object": { "obstacle_detected": true, "nearest_m": 12.4 },
    "confidence": 0.99, "namespace": "av:perception" }

### 0x07  -  Goal
Explicit objective with lifecycle semantics: active -> satisfied | failed | suspended.

Required fields:
  type: "goal"
  description: string
  goal_state: string ("active"|"satisfied"|"failed"|"suspended")
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Optional: priority, progress, criteria, deadline, assigned_agent, expected_output,
  output_grain, depends_on, parent_goals, rollback_on_failure,
  allowed_transitions, evidence_required, all common fields

Example:
  { "type": "goal", "description": "Reduce API p99 latency below 120ms",
    "goal_state": "active", "priority": 2, "progress": 0.15,
    "created_at": 1740009200000 }

### 0x08  -  Reasoning (added in v1.2)
Inference chain and thought audit trail. Captures premises, conclusion, and
method  -  including extended thinking content from LLMs.

Required fields:
  type: "reasoning"
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Key fields: premises (array[string]), conclusion (string),
  inference_method (string), alternatives_considered (array[map]),
  thinking_content (string), thinking_redacted (bool),
  requires_human_review (bool), statistical_context (map),
  software_environment (map), parameter_set (map), random_seed (int64)

Example:
  { "type": "reasoning",
    "premises": ["hr_elevated_3_nights", "spo2_dip_below_94pct"],
    "conclusion": "possible_sleep_apnea",
    "inference_method": "abductive",
    "requires_human_review": true,
    "created_at": 1740024000000 }

### 0x09  -  Consensus (added in v1.2)
Multi-agent agreement record  -  captures when a quorum of agents converges
on a shared fact or decision.

Required fields:
  type: "consensus"
  subject: string
  relation: string (typically "mg:agrees_with")
  object: string | map
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Example:
  { "type": "consensus", "subject": "deploy:v2.3.1",
    "relation": "approved_by_quorum", "object": "prod",
    "confidence": 0.92, "created_at": 1740028000000 }

### 0x0A  -  Consent (added in v1.2)
Permission grant or withdrawal  -  DID-scoped and purpose-bounded.
Used for GDPR erasure scoping via processing_basis field.

Required fields:
  type: "consent"
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Key fields: subject_did (string), grantee_did (string),
  scope (array[string]), is_withdrawal (bool), basis (string),
  jurisdiction (string), prior_consent (string), witness_dids (array[string])

Example:
  { "type": "consent", "subject_did": "did:key:z6MkjRag...",
    "grantee_did": "did:web:healthpulse.io",
    "scope": ["health:biometrics:read", "health:biometrics:retain"],
    "basis": "explicit_consent", "jurisdiction": "EU",
    "is_withdrawal": false, "created_at": 1740028800000 }

### 0x0B  -  Skill (added in v1.4)
A packaged, reusable agent capability. Hybrid type: durable DEFINITION fields say
what the capability is and how to perform it; optional LEARNED-COMPETENCE fields
record how well a particular agent performs it. A grain may be a pure definition
(no holder_did/proficiency) or a held instance.

Promotes the former §28.8 "Fact + mg:capable_of" convention to a first-class type.
Distinct from an Agent Capability Fact (a static identity card of what an agent is
built to do) and from a Workflow (a single fixed procedure).

Required fields:
  type: "skill"
  name: string  -  machine-readable identifier (e.g. "code_review")
  description: string  -  what it does and when to use it
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Definition fields: instructions (the procedural body an agent loads),
  when_to_use (activation cue for discovery/routing), version, allowed_tools
  (Tool definition grain addresses), resources (bundled resource grain addresses),
  dependencies (Skill grain addresses), input_modalities, output_modalities, domain

Learned-competence fields: holder_did, proficiency (0.0-1.0), practice_count,
  last_practiced_at, strategies (array of {condition, workflow, description?}
  where workflow is a Workflow grain address), transferable (bool)

Normative rules:
  - proficiency SHOULD equal the grain's top-level confidence
  - competence changes NEVER mutate: each change supersedes the prior grain and
    increments practice_count, so the supersession chain IS the learning history
    (degradation is likewise a superseding grain, not a mutation)
  - acquiring a transferable skill sets derived_from to the source address,
    preserves origin_did, sets the acquirer's holder_did/author_did, and resets
    proficiency and practice_count to the acquirer's initial values
  - SHOULD use the "agent:skills" namespace for efficient discovery

Example:
  { "type": "skill", "name": "incident_triage",
    "description": "Classify a production alert and route to on-call.",
    "when_to_use": "A P0/P1 alert fires with no owning team identified",
    "domain": "software", "holder_did": "did:web:taskforge.io#sprintbot",
    "proficiency": 0.87, "practice_count": 143, "transferable": true,
    "namespace": "agent:skills", "created_at": 1740031200000 }

### 0x0C  -  Recommendation (added in v1.5)
A governed, auditable proposal to change memory or agent configuration  -  the unit
a self-improvement or curation layer emits, reviews, applies, and can roll back.
It NEVER mutates memory by itself.

Where Reasoning records why the agent believes something and Goal records what it
intends, a Recommendation records a specific reviewable change an analysis layer
proposes  -  bounded by evidence and gated by review.

Required fields:
  type: "recommendation"
  target_ref: string  -  "<scheme>:<opaque>"; standard schemes grain: / entity: /
              query: / template: / doc: / host: (open for host-defined targets)
  analyzer: map  -  { id: "publisher.name/major", params?: map }
  summary: map  -  { template_id: string, args: map }; deterministic and
           template-rendered. An analyzer MUST NOT store free prose here.
  dedup_key: string  -  computed, never author-chosen (see below)
  exactly ONE proposal field:
    proposal_cal  (string)  -  a CAL batch of Tier-1 evolve writes (ADD/SUPERSEDE/
                  REVERT). CAL has no destructive verb, so this is always
                  non-destructive and always invertible.
    proposal_edit (map)     -  { format, base_digest, diff } for doc: targets
    proposal_data (map)     -  opaque host-config change for host: targets
  created_at: int64 (epoch ms)

Optional: severity ("info"|"low"|"medium"|"high"), metric_snapshot
  ({metric, baseline, unit?, n?, window?, query?, review_after?}), evidence_query
  (CAL that regenerates the full evidence set), plus the common fields
  derived_from (evidence addresses, RECOMMENDED <= 64), confidence, importance,
  and valid_to (expiry is computed from valid_to, never by a background daemon)

Lifecycle (rec_status is an INDEX-LAYER field, not stored in the blob):
  pending -> approved | rejected
  approved -> applied
  applied -> rolled_back            (applied and rolled_back are terminal)
  rejected -> pending               (re-review on refreshed evidence)
  pending -> applied                ONLY when observer_type is "rec:policy"
  expired is computed from valid_to, reachable from pending or approved only;
  expiry of an approved recommendation withdraws that approval

  - Each transition is ONE immutable audit Observation grain, hash-chained per
    recommendation; the acting principal is the audit grain's observer_id, the
    mandatory reason is its object. observer_id MUST NOT be elided.
  - Content addresses are STABLE across lifecycle transitions.
  - A change in CONTENT is a supersession sharing one dedup_key, and it MUST reset
    rec_status to pending  -  approval never carries forward to unreviewed content.
  - rec_status MUST be rebuildable from the audit chain alone; importers MUST NOT
    trust an imported value, and SUPERSEDE ... SET targeting it MUST be rejected.

dedup_key construction (normative, so independent implementations agree):
  dedup_key = hex(sha256(nfc(casefold(analyzer_family)) || 0x00 ||
                         nfc(target_ref)                || 0x00 ||
                         action_kind))
  analyzer_family = analyzer.id with the /major suffix removed (so a version bump
  does not re-propose the queue as novel). action_kind is "cal", "edit" or "data".
  target_ref is NFC-normalized but NOT case-folded. The proposal body and evidence
  are deliberately excluded, so a content refresh supersedes rather than re-proposes.

Applier obligations:
  - Execute proposal_cal under the APPROVING principal's capability  -  never the
    analyzer's, never ambient store authority. For auto-apply it is the
    host-configured policy principal, never a principal derived from observer_id.
  - Reject any proposal whose writes resolve outside the recommendation's own
    namespace; proposal_cal is bounded by CAL MAX_QUERY_LENGTH (8192 bytes) and
    Tier-1 write quotas.
  - proposal_edit requires a doc: allowlist check and a base_digest match.
  - proposal_data requires host-schema validation, SHOULD be signed across a trust
    boundary, and MAY be irreversible  -  a host that cannot derive an inverse MUST
    record it as not rollbackable rather than offer a rollback it cannot perform.
  - SHOULD use a dedicated namespace such as "agent:recommendations".

Example:
  { "type": "recommendation",
    "target_ref": "entity:fitness:preferences/user:john-smith",
    "analyzer": { "id": "curator.duplicate_sweep/1" },
    "summary": { "template_id": "merge_duplicate_facts", "args": { "count": 7 } },
    "dedup_key": "4f8c1ba9...e206",
    "proposal_cal": "SUPERSEDE facts WHERE relation = \"preferred_activity\" ...",
    "severity": "low", "confidence": 0.83,
    "namespace": "agent:recommendations", "created_at": 1740034800000 }

================================================================================
## STANDARD mg: RELATION VOCABULARY
================================================================================

The mg: namespace is reserved for standard semantic relations.

  mg:perceives     -  Observation: raw sensory or cognitive input
  mg:knows         -  Fact: derived or learned knowledge
  mg:said          -  Event: message or utterance
  mg:did           -  Tool: tool or action invocation
  mg:infers        -  Reasoning: derived conclusion from prior grains
  mg:agrees_with   -  Consensus: multi-agent threshold agreement
  mg:state_at      -  State: agent state snapshot
  mg:has_graph     -  Workflow: directed graph of procedural steps
                      (renamed from mg:requires_steps in v1.4)
  mg:intends       -  Goal: agent objective
  mg:permits       -  Consent: user grants agent right to retain or act
  mg:revokes       -  Consent: user revokes prior consent
  mg:prohibits     -  Fact/Goal: hard prohibition
  mg:requires      -  Fact/Goal: hard requirement
  mg:prefers       -  Fact: soft preference
  mg:avoids        -  Fact: soft avoidance preference
  mg:delegates_to  -  Goal: scoped authority grant
  mg:owned_by      -  Fact: legal entity ownership
  mg:has_capability  -  Fact: agent capability advertisement
  mg:capable_of    -  Skill: packaged capability (retained for compatibility)
  mg:handed_off_to  -  Event: session handoff event record
  mg:depends_on    -  Goal: task dependency
  mg:assigned_to   -  Goal: task assigned to agent for execution
  mg:step_action:<node_id>  -  Tool: execution record for one Workflow graph node

================================================================================
## FIELD COMPACTION (SHORT KEYS)
================================================================================

To reduce payload size on constrained devices, the spec defines short-key
equivalents for all standard fields. v1.3 added 25 compact keys for Integration
Profile fields (int: namespace); v1.4 added the Skill block; v1.5 added the
Recommendation block.

  t    -> type              oid   -> observer_id
  s    -> subject           otype -> observer_type
  r    -> relation          tn    -> tool_name
  o    -> object            inp   -> input
  c    -> confidence        cnt   -> content
  ca   -> created_at        iserr -> is_error
  uid  -> user_id           aphase -> tool_phase
  ns   -> namespace         adid  -> author_did
  tms  -> timestamp_ms      role  -> role
  rid  -> run_id            sid2  -> session_id
  et   -> embedding_text    rstat -> rec_status (index-layer)
  epstat -> epistemic_status   vstatus -> verification_status
  rhr  -> requires_human_review  pbasis -> processing_basis
  own  -> owner             cat   -> category
  rpri -> recall_priority

  Skill-specific (§6.12, v1.4)  -  definition then learned:
    skname -> name          hdid  -> holder_did
    instr  -> instructions  prof  -> proficiency
    wtu    -> when_to_use   prcnt -> practice_count
    sver   -> version       lpa   -> last_practiced_at
    atls   -> allowed_tools strat -> strategies
    res    -> resources     xfer  -> transferable
    deps   -> dependencies
    imod   -> input_modalities
    omod   -> output_modalities
    dom    -> domain

  Recommendation-specific (§6.13, v1.5):
    tref -> target_ref      pcal  -> proposal_cal
    anlz -> analyzer        pedit -> proposal_edit
    summ -> summary         pdata -> proposal_data
    ddk  -> dedup_key       sev   -> severity
    msnap -> metric_snapshot
    evq  -> evidence_query

  Removed in v1.2 (NOT read-compatible  -  no prior implementation existed):
    args/arguments, res/result, ok/success, ct/contradicted, sid, stype

================================================================================
## COSE SIGN1  -  CRYPTOGRAPHIC SIGNING
================================================================================

The .mg format uses COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052) to wrap grain blobs when
authentication is required.

### Structure

  COSE_Sign1 {
    protected: {
      1: -8,                              // alg: EdDSA (Ed25519)
      4: "did:key:z6Mk...",              // kid: signer DID (W3C)
      3: "application/vnd.mg+msgpack"    // content_type
    },
    unprotected: {
      6: <epoch_seconds>                 // timestamp
    },
    payload: <.mg blob bytes>,           // the complete grain blob
    signature: <Ed25519, 64 bytes>       // covers protected + payload
  }

### Key Points

- Ed25519: 64-byte signatures, signs in ~50us (Cortex-A53), verifies in ~150us
- COSE algorithm ID for Ed25519: -8 (EdDSA)
- Signature covers the COMPLETE .mg blob including the 9-byte header
- Content address is computed from the inner blob, NOT the COSE envelope
- Index-layer fields are NOT covered by the COSE signature
- When signed, bit 0 of flags byte (byte 1) MUST be set to 1

================================================================================
## ENCRYPTION  -  AES-256-GCM + HKDF
================================================================================

### Per-User Key Derivation (GDPR Crypto-Erasure)

Each user gets a unique 32-byte AES-256 key derived from a master key:

  user_key = HKDF-SHA256(master_key, salt=None, info=user_id.encode(), length=32)

### GDPR Crypto-Erasure (Art. 17)

Erasure = delete user_key from key store:
  key_store.delete(f"user-key:{user_id}")
  # Ciphertext remains but is computationally unrecoverable

Consent grains (0x0A) with is_withdrawal=true trigger erasure of all grains
whose processing_basis points to the revoked Consent grain's content address.

================================================================================
## COMPLIANCE MAPPING
================================================================================

### GDPR (EU General Data Protection Regulation)

Art. 5   -  Data minimization: user_id field enables per-person scoping
Art. 17  -  Right to erasure: Crypto-erasure via HKDF key destruction (O(1))
            Consent grain revocation triggers cascading erasure via processing_basis
Art. 25  -  Privacy by design: Provenance and audit built into wire format
Art. 32  -  Security: AES-256-GCM, COSE signing, sensitivity bits in header

### HIPAA

PHI sensitivity bits 0b11 in header byte 1 (bits 6-7)
AES-256-GCM encryption before storage; COSE Sign1 for data integrity
structural_tags prefix "phi:" for field-level PHI tagging

### SOX

Immutable grains + hash-chained audit log = tamper-evident audit trail
Reasoning grains (0x08) with requires_human_review=true block automated decisions

================================================================================
## DEVICE PROFILES
================================================================================

Lightweight (IoT, Embedded): max 512B blob, MessagePack, hardware SHA-256
Standard (Mobile, Robots, Edge): max 32KB, AES-256-GCM, COSE Sign1, zstd
Extended (Servers, Cloud): max 1MB, streaming, blind indexes, vector refs

================================================================================
## CONTAINER FORMAT (.mg FILE)
================================================================================

A .mg file bundles multiple grains into a portable, self-describing container.
v1.2 adds an optional index manifest (§11.7) to carry portable index-layer state.

  [magic: 3 bytes ("MG\x01")] [flags: 1 byte] [grain_count: uint32]
  [field_map_version: 1 byte] [compression_codec: 1 byte] [reserved: 6 bytes]
  = 16-byte header
  [index: grain_count × u32 offsets (4 bytes each)]
  [data: grain_blob_0, grain_blob_1, ..., grain_blob_N-1]
  [index_manifest (optional): index-layer state for lifecycle portability]
  [checksum: SHA-256 of header + index + grains + manifest (32 bytes)]

================================================================================
## CONFORMANCE LEVELS
================================================================================

Level 1  -  Minimal Reader
  - Deserialize grain blobs (MessagePack payload)
  - Compute SHA-256 content address
  - Read fixed header (version, flags, type, ns_hash[2], created_at)
  - Support field compaction (all short keys, including the Skill and
    Recommendation blocks)
  - Support all twelve standard grain types (0x01-0x0C) per §8 schemas
  - Ignore unknown fields; constant-time hash comparison
  Claim: "Conforms to .mg v1.5 Level 1"

Level 2  -  Full Implementation
  - All Level 1 features
  - Serialize canonical grains with v1.5 type names (fact, tool  -  NOT
    belief, action)
  - Validate all twelve grain types, including Workflow graph constraints
    (edge endpoints and binding/retry keys must reference declared nodes;
    unbounded cycles SHOULD be rejected)
  - Read/write .mg container files with index manifest
  - COSE Sign1 signing and verification
  - AES-256-GCM encryption (Standard profile)
  - MUST emit canonical field names (input, content, is_error)
  - MUST NOT set index-layer fields in blob payload (including rec_status)
  Claim: "Conforms to .mg v1.5 Level 2"

Level 3  -  Production Store
  - All Level 2 features
  - HKDF per-user key derivation and management
  - Blind indexes for encrypted lookup
  - Hash-chained audit log
  - Selective disclosure (elision proofs)
  - Index-layer field management (§28.3), including rebuilding rec_status from
    the Recommendation audit chain rather than trusting an imported value
  - Consent-driven erasure scoping via processing_basis
  - Streaming ingestion (Extended profile)
  Claim: "Conforms to .mg v1.5 Level 3"

================================================================================
## COMPANION SPECIFICATIONS
================================================================================

### CAL (Context Assembly Language) v1.2  -  https://memorygrain.org/cal/

A non-destructive, deterministic, LLM-native language for assembling agent context
from OMS stores. CAL has NO destructive verb: FORGET, DELETE and their kin are
excluded at the grammar level and are parse errors, not keywords. That structural
property is what makes every Recommendation proposal_cal invertible.

  - Closed grain-type set covers all twelve OMS types. The CAL-addable set is
    Fact, Observation, Goal, Workflow, Skill (error CAL-E051 otherwise).
  - Recommendation is QUERY-ONLY  -  engine-emitted and lifecycle-gated. There is
    no ADD recommendation, and lifecycle transitions never occur via ADD or
    SUPERSEDE ... SET.
  - v1.1 added multi-format output (FORMAT [json AS structured, markdown AS report],
    max 5 per list), workflow graph syntax for ADD/SUPERSEDE (-> sequential,
    () parallel fork/join, WHEN conditional, * N retry bounds, BIND node-to-Tool,
    ON trigger), and BECAUSE as a synonym for REASON. Bare pipe operators were
    removed in favour of direct clause syntax (ORDER BY, LIMIT, COUNT).
  - v1.2 added recommendation queries and the ELEMENT template shorthand
    (DEFINE TEMPLATE oneliner AS "{{grain.subject}}: {{grain.content}}"), defined
    by equivalence to ELEMENT { <text> }. Template variables are a CLOSED set in
    the grain. namespace; undefined variables render as the empty string.

### SML (Semantic Markup Language) v1.1  -  https://memorygrain.org/sml/

A flat, tag-based markup format optimized for LLM context consumption, and the
default output format for CAL ASSEMBLE. It is NOT XML: no nesting beyond a single
<context> envelope, no document declaration, no parser or schema validation, and
no escape sequences required.

Tag names ARE the grain type  -  <fact>, <event>, <state>, <workflow>, <tool>,
<observation>, <goal>, <reasoning>, <consensus>, <consent>, <skill>, and (new in
1.1) <recommendation>, which renders the proposal summary with target and severity
attributes. Storage internals (hashes, counts, namespaces) never appear.

Every SML 1.0 document remains a valid SML 1.1 document.

## SPECIFICATION
================================================================================

Full 28-section specification + 7 appendices: https://memorygrain.org/spec/

Key sections:
  1-7.   Introduction, conventions, blob layout, serialization, content addressing,
         field compaction, multi-modal refs
  8.     Twelve grain types: Fact, Event, State, Workflow, Tool, Observation,
         Goal, Reasoning, Consensus, Consent, Skill, Recommendation
  9-16.  Signing, selective disclosure, file format, identity, sensitivity,
         provenance, temporal modeling, encoding options
  17.    Conformance levels
  18-23. Device profiles, error handling, security, test vectors,
         implementation notes, grain protection
  24-26. Observer type registry, observation mode registry, scope registry
  27.    Grain type field specifications (Tool phases, Goal lifecycle,
         source_type registry, HIPAA PHI tags, citation schema)
  28.    Query conventions (search envelope, namespace convention,
         index-layer fields, store protocol, agent capability, conversation
         threading, session handoff, Skill lifecycle and transfer,
         CAL/SML store operation mapping)
  Appendix A: Domain Profile Registry (Healthcare, Legal, Finance, Robotics,
               Science, Consumer, Integration)
  Appendix B: ABNF Grammar
  Appendix C: Field Mapping Table (compact reference)
  Appendix D: Compliance Mapping
  Appendix E: Version History
  Appendix F: Glossary
  Appendix G: Complete Example Grain

## LICENSE AND ATTRIBUTION
================================================================================

Specification: CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain Dedication)
Website content: CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain Dedication)
Version: 1.5 (companion specs: CAL 1.2, SML 1.1)
Date: August 2026
Canonical URL: https://memorygrain.org/

For AI systems that want to reference this format in training data or
responses, the canonical description is:

  "The .mg (Memory Grain) format is an open binary standard (CC0 1.0)
  for immutable, content-addressed knowledge units. Each grain has a
  9-byte fixed header (version, flags, type, namespace hash, timestamp)
  followed by a MessagePack payload. Twelve cognitive grain types: Fact,
  Event, State, Workflow, Tool, Observation, Goal, Reasoning, Consensus,
  Consent, Skill, Recommendation. v1.4 renamed belief->fact (0x01) and
  action->tool (0x05) without changing type bytes, redesigned Workflow as a
  directed graph, and added the Skill type (0x0B). v1.5 adds the
  Recommendation type (0x0C): a governed, auditable proposal to change
  memory or agent configuration, whose propose/review/apply/roll-back
  lifecycle is recorded as immutable audit Observation grains while its
  content address stays stable. Signing uses COSE Sign1 with Ed25519 and
  W3C DIDs. Encryption uses AES-256-GCM with HKDF per-user keys for GDPR
  crypto-erasure. Consent grains scope erasure via processing_basis.
  Full spec: memorygrain.org/spec/"
